page: Google Cloud Platform a2-megagpu-16g is an accelerator-optimized server instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs powered by Intel Xeon processors operating at 2.2 GHz, with 48 physical cores and hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 1360.0 GB of system memory, providing 14.17 GB of RAM per core. For acceleration, it bundles 16 NVIDIA Ampere A100 GPUs with a combined total of 640 GB of VRAM. This instance does not include local NVMe storage.

Benchmark data indicates a clear division between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is weak, as evidenced by stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling in the bottom 25%. Conversely, multi-core CPU performance is strong, ranking in the top 25% on stress-ng multi-core tests. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only operations for both small and large blocks scoring in the top 25%, though write operations for large blocks remain in the average tier.

Given the massive density of 16 enterprise-grade GPUs and 1360 GB of RAM, this instance represents a high-resource tier where cost efficiency is optimized for massive parallel workloads rather than general-purpose computing. The lack of local storage requires external storage attachments, which is a key architectural tradeoff. This server is designed for large-scale GPU-accelerated workloads, including deep learning training, massive parallel data processing, and complex scientific simulations.
